subject: English
question_text: Complete the text adding suffixes, prefixes or the both with the root words given in the parenthesis.
stimulus: 0.5  10 = 5 Last October in 2022, the United States Bureau of Industry and Security issued a document that (a) under its 139 pages of dense (b) bureau jargon and minute (c) tech detail amounted to a declaration of economic war on China. The magnitude of the act was made all the more remarkable by the relative (d) obscure of its source. One of 13 bureaus within the Department of Commerce, the (e) small federal department by funding, B.I.S. is tiny. In recent years, (f) conductor chips have become central to the bureau’s work. Yet beneath China’s strength is a crucial (g) vulnerable. Nearly all the chips that power the country’s most advanced projects and institutions are (h) inevitable tied to U.S. technology, as Chip War reveals, China, which spends more money importing chips than any other product, is pouring billions into a chip-building (i) initiate to catch the US’s lead. At stake is not only America’s economic prosperity but also its military (j) superior.
guide_solution: Adding suffix, prefix or both (a) underneath (b) bureaucratic (c) technical (d) obscurity (e) smallest (f) semiconductor (g) vulnerability (h) inevitably (i) initiative (j) superiority
